results.title: Korean edtech startup sees AI transform how students are assessed
results.content: Teachers are spending increasing amounts of time grading assignments and handling administrative work, leaving less time for students, but a Korean education technology startup believes artificial intelligence (AI) can help change that equation. Hyperlearning, an AI-powered education technology company specializing in assessment, is developing tools that automate grading, generate examination questions and provide personalized feedback, with ambitions to expand from Korea into Southeast Asia and the United States. Its co-founder and CEO Lim Chae-won believes AI should do more than make existing assessment methods faster. He argues that technology should fundamentally change how educators evaluate students and understand their abilities. “In the age of AI, the way we assess students and the very paradigm of educational assessment should be changed,” Lim said in an interview with The Korea

results.title: Korea to ground flights for 35 minutes during CSAT English test Thursday
results.content: Korea will suspend aircraft takeoffs nationwide for 35 minutes Thursday as students sit for the English listening section of the annual college entrance exam, with 130 flights facing schedule changes. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said Tuesday that aircraft will be prohibited from taking off between 1:05 p.m. to 1:40 p.m., when the listening test for the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) will be administered. The measure is intended to eliminate aircraft noise that could interfere with students' concentration during one of the exam's most closely monitored sections. Aircraft already in the air will be required to remain at least 3 kilometers above ground during the restricted period. Emergency and other urgent flights will be exempt. results.title: Veteran actress Lee Young-ae stuns alongside K-pop girl group aespa
results.content: Veteran Korean actress Lee Young-ae, 55, is drawing attention for her seemingly ageless appearance after sharing photos of herself alongside K-pop girl group aespa at the 2026 Melon Music Awards (MMA). On Tuesday, Lee posted several photos on her personal social media account, offering a behind-the-scenes glimpse of her appearance at the music awards ceremony. "It's been a long time since I stood on the stage at a music awards ceremony," she wrote. In the photos, Lee poses backstage in an elegant green off-the-shoulder gown featuring a fitted bodice and a voluminous skirt. The dress accentuates her slender figure and sophisticated style. One photo in particular shows Lee standing alongside the four members of aespa in a waiting room. results.title: Complaint filed against education minister for dereliction of duty over AI cheating
results.content: A former Seoul city councilor filed a complaint against Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin on Tuesday, accusing him of dereliction of duty after the minister said it would be difficult to catch all forms of cheating using artificial intelligence (AI). Lee Jong-bae, a former Seoul city council member from the main opposition People Power Party, said he submitted the complaint to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency over the remarks Choi made during a plenary session of the National Assembly's education committee the previous day when questioned about AI-assisted cheating. The move came amid heightened public anxiety over such misconduct ahead of Thursday's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), an annual national college entrance exam, known as Suneung in Korean. results.title: Korea regains top spot in global OLED shipments in H1
results.content: Korea regained the top spot in the global organic light-emitting diode (OLED) market by shipment volume in the first half of this year, overtaking China for the first time in two years, industry data showed Tuesday. Korea accounted for 50.1 percent of global OLED shipments in the first half, narrowly surpassing China's 49.8 percent, according to data compiled by the Korea Display Industry Association (KDIA). In terms of revenue, Korea's share of the global OLED market rose 3 percentage points on-year to 68.3 percent, while China's market share fell to 31.7 percent from 34.5 percent a year earlier. Korea's revenue-based market share increased for the third consecutive year, following 64.2 percent in 2024 and 65.3 percent in 2025.

results.title: Sejong Center's outdoor garden transforms into winter market
results.content: A popular garden in central Seoul is trading autumn jazz for Christmas lights, hot snacks and handmade gifts. Sejong Center for the Performing Arts said Tuesday that Curtain Call Garden will reopen as a winter market from Tuesday through Jan. 3 in its Art Garden courtyard, operating daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. The seasonal transformation will bring traditional winter treats, warm drinks, crafts and holiday decorations to the space, which opened in October as part of Seoul's initiative to stimulate nighttime economic activity. Visitors can buy fish-shaped pastries, caramel-filled fried doughnuts, roasted sweet potatoes and savory fish cake from Happy Carp Bread, while Tea Tree Vin Chaud will serve warm mulled wine and highballs. results.title: 2026 Korea Times Forum
results.content: The Korea Times will host a forum titled "Capital market advancement: Giant leap toward era of Korea premium" on Nov. 24. The event will take place from 9 a.m. to 11:50 a.m. at the Grand Hall of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry in central Seoul. Korea's capital market stands at a pivotal moment as it moves beyond the "Korea discount" toward an era of "Korea premium." While government-led reforms and the artificial intelligence boom have laid the groundwork for this transition, strengthening global competitiveness and investor confidence remains a key challenge. Bringing together policymakers, financial market experts and business leaders from Korea and abroad, the forum will serve as a platform to exchange insights and explore strategies for the future of Korea's capital market. results.title: Min Hee-jin denies influencing NewJeans' contract termination after police refer breach of trust case to prosecutors
results.content: Former ADOR CEO Min Hee-jin has denied allegations that she influenced K-pop girl group NewJeans to terminate its exclusive contract with the agency, after police referred her to prosecutors on suspicion of breach of trust. Ooak Records, the agency currently headed by Min, said in an official statement Monday that Min had played no role in prompting the group's decision to end its contract with ADOR. "Min did not exercise any influence whatsoever to induce NewJeans to decide to terminate its contract," the company said. Min's side pointed to an earlier decision by Seoul's Yongsan Police Station not to refer a separate case involving allegations of occupational breach of trust and an attempted takeover of management control to prosecutors. results.title: Lee urges stronger ASEAN+3 role as regional shocks spread
results.content: MANILA, Philippines — President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday urged ASEAN Plus Three, a regional cooperation framework comprising the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) plus Korea, China and Japan, to strengthen its role in tackling shared crises as conflicts and economic shocks increasingly spill across borders. results.title: Sungkyunkwan University holds global living lab on AI-driven traffic solutions
results.content: Sungkyunkwan University held the final presentation session of a global living lab project at its Seoul campus on Nov. 5, showcasing student-led efforts to address urban transportation challenges using artificial intelligence (AI) and geospatial technologies. Organized by the university’s ANCHOR Project Group in collaboration with Jeonbuk National University, the second Global Livinglab: AI×Traffic System aimed to help students tackle real-world urban problems through interdisciplinary research and practical problem-solving. The initiative also sought to nurture industry-ready talent in the future mobility sector by combining universities’ educational and research capabilities with the expertise of public institutions and industry partners. results.title: Top scorer of tax accountant exam apologizes for cheating before police questioning
results.content: The top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam apologized Tuesday for cheating on the test as he appeared before police to undergo questioning. The man, surnamed Han, admitted Sunday to using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative artificial intelligence (AI) to score top marks on the exam, sparking public outcry and concerns over cheating in national exams. "I am truly sorry to those who prepared for the exam and those involved," he told reporters at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's office in western Seoul. "I will not hide what I did and will tell the truth to investigative authorities." He said he would take responsibility for his actions but did not answer questions about whether he acted alone and how he prepared the equipment to cheat on the test. results.title: N. Korea's Kim inspects tourism development site near China ahead of Trump's Asia trip
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has inspected a tourist zone development site near China, Pyongyang's state media reported Tuesday, ahead of U.S. President Donald Trump's trip to China for a regional summit amid speculation that he may seek dialogue with Kim. Kim toured the site in Samjiyon, Ryanggang Province, on Sunday and Monday, highlighting the economic and cultural importance of developing tourism resources, including Mount Paektu, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). The report confirmed that Kim was in the border city as Trump plans to visit Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit set for Wednesday and Thursday. Before embarking on his Asia trip, Trump told reporters that he may meet Kim in China this week. results.title: From metal detectors to eyeglass checks, US exams confront AI cheating
results.content: SEATTLE — For Americans taking high-stakes professional licensing exams, security checks can resemble those at an airport. At Prometric testing centers, which administer examinations for aspiring physicians and certified public accountants (CPA), candidates must undergo metal detector screening, turn their pockets inside out and raise their sleeves and pant legs before entering the examination room. Eyeglasses are also removed for inspection to ensure they do not conceal recording devices. The entire security screening process is repeated after every break, according to Prometric's published testing policies. Such stringent precautions illustrate how some U.S. testing centers guard against concealed electronic devices, an issue that has taken on new urgency in Korea ahead of Thursday's national college entrance examination, one of the country's most consequential academic tests. results.title: Upstage teams up with Canada's Cohere for sovereign AI solutions
results.content: Korean artificial intelligence (AI) startup Upstage said Tuesday it will collaborate with Canadian AI firm Cohere to develop sovereign AI solutions and expand into the global enterprise AI market. Under the strategic partnership, Upstage will integrate its large language models, Solar Pro and Solar Mini, and its document processing platform, Document Parse, with Cohere's enterprise AI agent platform, North. The combined solution will be offered through locally installed systems and cloud-based virtual private clouds (VPCs), targeting businesses and institutions with strict data security and regulatory requirements. The two companies also plan to expand their partnership beyond Korea into the broader Asia-Pacific region, focusing on enterprise AI solutions that allow organizations to maintain control over their data.

results.title: N. Korean leader's close aide meets senior officials in Moscow amid deepening ties
results.content: A senior North Korean official and a close aide to leader Kim Jong-un has met Russia's top party and parliamentary figures in Moscow, according to Pyongyang's state media Tuesday, amid deepening ties between the two countries. Jo Yong-won, a secretary of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), met Dmitry Medvedev, chairman of the United Russia Party, and Vyacheslav Volodin, speaker of the State Duma of Russia, on Monday, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said, citing Russia's Tass news agency. Talks with Medvedev centered on deepening "strategic and tactical cooperation" under the agreements the two countries' leaders signed in June 2024. With Volodin, the two sides discussed further promoting "inter-parliamentary dialogue," according to the report. results.title: Seoul stocks sharply down late Tuesday morning amid lingering AI woes
results.content: South Korean stocks traded sharply lower late Tuesday morning, amid lingering concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investment ahead of Nvidia's earnings report and Anthropic's stock market debut. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) lost 63.04 points, or 1.24 percent, to 5,037.46 as of 11:20 a.m., after falling as low as 4,984.83. The index retreated for the fourth consecutive session. On Wall Street, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped about 2.5 percent Monday (U.S. time), while AI chip giant Nvidia slid 4.1 percent amid continued uncertainty following the departure of its CEO, Jensen Huang, last week. Nvidia is scheduled to report its earnings Tuesday (U.S. time), with investors closely watching its outlook for AI chip demand and infrastructure spending. results.title: How AI should change job interviews
results.content: About 100 technology companies attended the Seoul Job Fair on Nov. 9, and around 60 planned to recruit some 400 people. Visitors used artificial intelligence (AI)-based job matching, met recruiters and explored a culture-fit test. These tools may help people navigate opportunities. However, the decisive hiring question is whether applicants can recognize when a persuasive AI recommendation is wrong. Korean employers are asking for more AI-related skills. In October, The Korea Times reported a 170 percent year-over-year increase in recruitment postings mentioning tools such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, according to JobKorea data. results.title: Hyundai Motor's plant utilization rate falls in Jan.-Sept. period
results.content: Hyundai Motor's global plant utilization rate fell in the first nine months of this year as vehicle production declined despite increased manufacturing capacity, corporate data showed Tuesday. The South Korean automaker's overall plant utilization rate stood at 86.1 percent in the January-September period, down from 94.3 percent a year earlier, according to its quarterly report. Total production capacity rose 3 percent on-year to 3.17 million vehicles, while actual output fell 6 percent to 2.73 million units. The combined utilization rate of its eight overseas plants dropped to 80.7 percent from 88.5 percent a year earlier. Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in the U.S. state of Georgia recorded the steepest decline, with its utilization rate plunging to 41.4 percent from 68.1 percent over the period. results.title: Samsung Electronics, SK hynix cash holdings surge amid AI-driven chip boom
results.content: The combined cash holdings of South Korean chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have more than doubled over the past year, driven by strong chip demand amid a global artificial intelligence (AI) boom, corporate filings showed Tuesday. The two chipmakers' combined cash, cash equivalents and short-term financial instruments reached 329.23 trillion won ($246.33 billion) as of the end of September, up from 136.3 trillion won a year earlier, according to their quarterly reports. The figure also rose sharply from 277.91 trillion won at the end of June, an increase of 51.32 trillion won in just three months. The sharp increase in cash holdings comes as the two chipmakers benefit from strong demand for high bandwidth memory (HBM) and other advanced memory chips used in AI data centers. results.content: Second Vice Foreign Minister Kim Jina has met with a senior U.S. State Department official and discussed cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI) and broader bilateral economic ties, Seoul's foreign ministry said Tuesday. The talks between Kim and U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg took place in San Francisco on Monday (local time), according to the ministry. Kim emphasized South Korea's broad capabilities across the AI value chain and its readiness to work with the United States and other partner countries. She also explained the objectives of South Korea's AI Basic Act and outlined plans for major projects involving semiconductors, data centers and physical AI, including efforts to match companies for cooperation. results.title: Several Russian military aircraft enter S. Korea's air defense zone without notice: JCS
results.content: Several Russian military aircraft briefly entered South Korea's air defense identification zone (KADIZ) early Tuesday, prompting the Air Force to deploy fighter jets in response, Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said. The South Korean military detected the Russian aircraft before they entered the KADIZ and deployed fighter jets to prepare for any possible contingencies, the JCS said in a statement. The aircraft later exited the zone without violating South Korea's airspace, it added. The air defense zone is not territorial airspace but is delineated to call on foreign planes to identify themselves so as to prevent accidental clashes. Russia and China, however, do not recognize the jurisdiction over KADIZ, citing a lack of basis in international law. results.title: Korea University brings together global leaders at THE Innovation & Impact Summit
results.content: Seoul is the stage this week for a global conversation on turning university research into commercial and social value. The Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026, held at Korea University from Tuesday to Thursday, brings together leading figures from higher education, research and industry to explore how universities can deepen ties with businesses and investors, foster entrepreneurship and move academic breakthroughs from the lab to the market. Under the theme “Universities, industry and investors: Connecting research with commercialisation,” the summit examines the expanding role of universities in driving technological progress and economic growth.

results.title: As Google Maps improves in Korea, Naver, Kakao turn to ecosystems to defend turf
results.content: Naver and Kakao are doubling down on local business listings, user reviews and services linking place discovery to bookings and payments to defend their positions in Korea's mapping market as Google prepares to introduce walking and driving directions in the country early next year. The U.S. tech giant is moving closer to launching the features after making progress in securing permission to use high-precision map data overseas. A government committee on Friday reviewed Google’s compliance with security requirements attached to the conditional approval for exporting 1:5,000-scale map data. With Google a step closer to offering more advanced location-based services in Korea, the move poses a new challenge to domestic platforms that have built their mapping businesses around local information and services extending beyond navigation. results.title: Sookmyung University redefines women's education for rapidly evolving AI era
results.content: Sookmyung Women’s University is redefining its role in higher education by integrating humanistic values into advanced engineering, life sciences and artificial intelligence (AI) to promote interdisciplinary research. Founded in 1906 by the Korean imperial court, the university has played a leading role in women's education, helping elevate women’s status in society and nurture future generations of female leaders. Marking its 120th anniversary this year, the university aims to cultivate a new generation of talent capable of challenging conventional thinking and forging new paths under its “Sookmyung Outthinkers” vision. “Sookmyung has pioneered innovative approaches to education, building on its 120-year tradition of women’s education and helping students realize their potential on a broader stage,” said Moon Si-yeun, president of the university. “We will continue to provide strong supp

results.title: Chonnam National University positions itself as key partner in Korea's 2nd semiconductor cluster
results.content: Chonnam National University (CNU) is stepping up efforts to become a globally recognized research university as plans move forward to establish the country’s second major semiconductor cluster in Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City. Under the government-led project, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, two leading Korean semiconductor companies, plan to invest a combined 800 trillion won ($590 billion) to build four memory plants on the site of a former military airport. The region offers several advantages, including available production sites, an electricity self-sufficiency rate of 170 percent and the nation’s largest renewable energy infrastructure. The biggest remaining challenge, however, is securing the more than 23,000 skilled professionals needed to operate the four fabs. results.title: Jeonbuk National University accelerates AI-driven education transformation
results.content: Jeonbuk National University is advancing an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven transformation in education and research to improve students’ learning experiences and prepare them for future careers. Its student-centered approach combines academic flexibility, AI-powered learning support and programs linking classroom study with industry needs. The university’s efforts have been recognized in the Korean Standard-Service Quality Index survey conducted by the Korean Standards Association. In 2026, the university ranked first among regional national universities for the eighth consecutive year, marking its 11th first-place finish since it first received the recognition in 2012. results.content: Sungkyunkwan University has emerged as a globally recognized research-intensive institution, combining its six-century tradition of educating the nation’s leaders with cutting-edge innovation. The 628-year-old university traces its roots to Sungkyunkwan, the highest state educational institution of the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910), which opended Hanyang, now Seoul, in 1398. Today, that rich academic heritage extends into advanced technology and industry-academia collaboration, the university said. Building on a three-decade partnership with Samsung Group, the university has strengthened ties between academia and industry through specialized educational programs and industry-linked departments, training professionals for emerging industries. “For more than six centuries, Sungkyunkwan has educated the leaders each era needed.
